gold_references.title: Pressure Vessels with Reinforced Heads
independent_claims: 1. A pressure vessel comprising an inner vessel formed by a cylindrical middle part, two arched vessel heads which respectively close the middle part on both sides, and an outer layer wound around the inner vessel for reinforcing the inner vessel against pressure loads, wherein the outer layer comprises at least one vessel head reinforcing layer made of a fiber composite material and a pressure vessel reinforcing layer, wherein the vessel head reinforcing layer at least partially covers the vessel head, the pressure vessel reinforcing layer covers the vessel head and the middle part, and a contour-stable preform serving as the vessel head reinforcing layer is provided on at least one of the vessel heads; the prefabricated member with the stable contour is formed by weaving fiber materials, the weaving angle of the fiber materials on the edge of the end socket of the prefabricated member is 160 degrees, one or more reinforcing ribs are woven into the woven prefabricated member, and the direction of the reinforcing ribs is basically parallel to the cylinder axis in the middle of the cylinder.
2. The pressure vessel of claim 1, wherein the dimensionally stable preform is made of a fibrous material stitched to a clothable carrier material.

3. A pressure vessel according to claim 2, wherein one or more reinforcing bars are sewn together on the carrier material, the direction of the reinforcing bars being substantially parallel to the axis of the cylindrical central portion.
gold_references.arrangement_analysis: The prior-art patent CN107850259B discloses a pressure vessel with a specific arrangement of layers and reinforcing elements, whereas the invention claim describes a hydrogel coating with a hydrogel matrix reinforced with nanofibers. The arrangement of the elements in the prior-art patent is unrelated to the invention's elements, specifically the hydrogel matrix and nanofibers. Therefore, the required arrangement of the invention's elements is not disclosed in the prior-art patent.
gold_references.relevance_assessment: The patent is about pressure vessels with reinforced heads, which is a completely different technology from the hydrogel coating invention. The use of fiber composite materials and reinforcement is not directly related to the hydrogel coating invention.

gold_references.title: Fiber Reinforced Resin Matrix Composite Cylinder Connection Structure
independent_claims: 1. The utility model provides a fiber reinforcement resin matrix combined material barrel connection structure, includes combined material barrel (1), its characterized in that: the composite material barrel is characterized by further comprising a metal connector (2) and fibers (3) wound in the circumferential direction, first connecting parts with outer ends shrinking inwards are formed at two end parts of the composite material barrel (1), the metal connector (2) comprises a pipe column and a second connecting part which are combined with each other and are in a dovetail shape, a baffle ring is arranged at the joint of the pipe column and the second connecting part, a groove-shaped fiber winding area (5) is formed between the baffle ring and the second connecting part, the outer side surface of the second connecting part and the side surface of the baffle ring opposite to the second connecting part are respectively provided with ring grooves (4) distributed at intervals, the first connecting part of the composite material cylinder body (1) is sleeved outside the second connecting part of the metal connector (2) in a matching way, the fiber winding device is characterized in that the fiber winding area (5) is filled with the circumferential winding fibers (3), and the composite material cylinder body (1), the metal connector (2) and the circumferential winding fibers (3) are of an integrally formed structure.

2. The fiber reinforced resin based composite material cylinder connection structure according to claim 1, wherein: the composite material cylinder (1), the metal connector (2) and the circumferential winding fibers (3) are integrally formed by a mould pressing method, a hot pressing tank method, a resin transfer molding method or a vacuum bag method.

3. The fiber reinforced resin based composite material cylinder connection structure according to claim 1, wherein: the matrix of the composite material cylinder (1) and/or the circumferential winding fiber (3) is cyanate ester resin, phenolic resin, epoxy resin, bismaleimide resin, benzoxazine resin or polyimide resin, and the reinforcement is carbon fiber, glass fiber, Kevlar fiber, quartz fiber, basalt fiber, ceramic fiber, boron fiber or plant fiber.
gold_references.arrangement_analysis: The prior-art patent CN110925276A discloses a fiber reinforcement resin matrix combined material barrel connection structure, which includes a composite material barrel, a metal connector, and circumferential winding fibers. However, the arrangement of these elements is specific to a barrel connection structure, whereas the invention claim is about a hydrogel coating comprising a hydrogel matrix reinforced with nanofibers. The arrangement of elements in the prior-art patent is not applicable to the invention's claimed subject matter, as it involves a different type of material and structure.
gold_references.relevance_assessment: The prior-art patent is about a fiber-reinforced resin matrix composite material cylinder connection structure, which is unrelated to the invention claim about a hydrogel coating reinforced with nanofibers.

workarounds.description: Replace the nanofibers with microfibers, which are larger in diameter and may not provide the same level of mechanical strength enhancement as nanofibers. However, they can still provide some level of reinforcement.
workarounds.value_preservation_analysis: The competitor may still achieve some level of mechanical strength enhancement, but it will likely be less effective than the original nanofibers. The economic value of the invention is still preserved, but the competitor's product may not be as competitive.

workarounds.description: Use a different hydrogel matrix that does not require nanofibers for reinforcement. This could be a hydrogel matrix that is inherently more robust or has a different chemical structure that makes it less susceptible to polymer chain scission.
workarounds.value_preservation_analysis: The competitor can still achieve the commercial value of the invention by using a different hydrogel matrix that provides the same level of mechanical strength and resistance to polymer chain scission.

workarounds.description: Add external reinforcement to the hydrogel coating, such as a layer of a rigid material or a mesh of fibers. This can provide additional mechanical strength and resistance to polymer chain scission.
workarounds.value_preservation_analysis: The competitor can still achieve the commercial value of the invention by adding external reinforcement to the hydrogel coating.

workarounds.description: Use a different material for the nanofibers, such as a polymer that is not as effective at enhancing the mechanical strength of the hydrogel matrix.
workarounds.value_preservation_analysis: The competitor may still achieve some level of mechanical strength enhancement, but it will likely be less effective than the original nanofibers. The economic value of the invention is still preserved, but the competitor's product may not be as competitive.

workarounds.description: Remove the hydrogel matrix reinforcement altogether, resulting in a hydrogel coating that is not reinforced with nanofibers.
workarounds.value_preservation_analysis: The competitor's product will not have the same level of mechanical strength and resistance to polymer chain scission as the original invention, and may not be competitive in the market.
